highlights.title: Home screen redesign (Layout v2)
changes: The home screen now uses fixed-height zones so the chart is the only flexible area.
Updated visual style and glass UI refresh the header, panels, bottom banner, and tab bar.
A single multi-use bottom panel shows the highest-priority state and allows tap-through actions while keeping stats in.
The glucose chart is now interactive with drag, momentum panning, pinch-to-zoom, double-tap presets, and press-and-hold.

highlights.title: Interactive home chart with pinch, pan, and scrub
changes: The main Home chart is now draggable and pans smoothly with momentum when you swipe it.
You can pinch to zoom the chart between short and long windows and double-tap to cycle zoom presets.
Press-and-hold on the chart shows a selection popover so you can inspect and scrub exact values.
Pulling the dashboard down forces a refresh/loop and shows an inline refresh indicator.
Basal bars now hang from the top of their pane and basal schedule visuals update after profile changes.

highlights.title: 72-hour chart and smoother zoom
changes: The home chart now shows up to 72 hours of history when opened.
Charts render only the visible time span plus padding to keep panning and zooming responsive.
You can pinch-zoom in to 1 hour, with smoother previews that snap to stable zoom steps.
When auto-following, the current glucose reading stays visible at tight zoom levels.
The Time in Range banner now shows 'today', and midnight x-axis ticks include day labels.

highlights.title: Multi-use home panel replaces stats banner
changes: The home stats banner is replaced by one multi-use panel that defaults to showing real time-in-range stats.
Panel banners respond to taps across their full area.
If notifications are disabled the panel shows a critical warning and opens the app Settings when tapped.
If CGM data is stale the panel shows a No Recent Glucose banner that opens a manual glucose entry sheet.
If the pump clock differs or Max IOB is zero the panel shows warnings that open pump setup or deep-link to the Max IOB.

highlights.title: Immediate stop of crash uploads on opt-out
changes: When you turn off Diagnostics, any crash reports waiting to be sent are deleted and stop uploading.
After opting out, the app no longer starts Firebase services so no new diagnostic data is re‑queued or sent.
Turning Diagnostics back on re-enables Firebase and allows diagnostic reporting to resume immediately.

includedPullRequests.body:
Part 1 of 7 of the home layout v2 series.

Introduces the zone architecture for the home dashboard: fixed-height slots for header, meal row, and bottom controls (`HomeLayout` constants), with the chart as the only flexible zone taking the remaining height. Bottom controls move into a `safeAreaInset` so the tab bar can never cover them; dashboard type size is capped at XXL so the fixed zones cannot bust.

State changes (banner, badge, bolus bar) no longer reflow the layout. Verified on SE3, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max simulators.

No visual changes of the home view.

includedPullRequests.body:
Part 4 of 7 of the home layout v2 series, stacked on `home-refactor-multiuse-panel`.

Makes the main chart interactive: offset-based panning with momentum, pinch zoom (2–24 h), double-tap zoom presets, hold-to-scrub selection popover, and pull-down-to-force-loop with an inline refresh indicator. includedPullRequests.title: [Part 5 of 7] Home Layout v2 – Extend chart history to 72h with windowed rendering
includedPullRequests.body:
Part 5 of 7 of the home layout v2 series, stacked on `home-refactor-chart-gestures`.

Extends chart history to 72 hours: all chart-feeding fetch controllers take span-aware predicates anchored at `chartHistoryStartDate`, re-anchored on foregrounding, with windowed rendering keeping only the visible span plus padding in the plot. The initially prototyped lazy backfill was dropped after real-device testing (visible load hitch) in favor of always loading 72 h. The TIR banner is labeled "today" to distinguish its daily scope from the 72 h chart.

Verified on device with 90 days of data and on the sims.

includedPullRequests.title: Home Layout v2
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

This integrates **Home Layout v2**, a fully refactored version of Trio's home screen as tracked in #1350, into `dev`. It brings in the seven-part stacked series that was developed and reviewed on the `feat/home-refactor` branch (#1326–#1332):

- **Zoning (#1326)** — fixed-height zones (header / meal row / bottom controls) with the chart as the only flexible zone. Bottom controls sit in a `safeAreaInset` so the tab bar can't cover them, and dashboard type size is capped, so badges, banners, and the bolus indicator no longer reflow the layout.
- **Layout rework (#1327)** — restyled header, panels, meal row, and the bottom stats banner.
- **Multi-use bottom panel (#1328)** — one slot where the highest-priority state wins: notifications-disabled → pump time mismatch → stale/missing CGM → Max IOB = 0 → today's statistics as the default face. Replaces the old stack of competing banners and gives each attention-state a consistent, non-blocking tap-through action. Statistics stay reachable via a fallback item in the History toolbar.
- **Interactive chart (#1329)** — draggable panning with momentum, pinch-to-zoom (1–24 h), double-tap presets, press-and-hold scrub-to-inspect, and pull-down-to-force-loop, replacing the fixed time-interval buttons.
- **72 h history (#1330)** — windowed rendering draws only the visible span plus padding, so the longer history doesn't cost per-frame layout.
- **Sensor lifecycle arc (#1331)** — the CGM arc now counts down toward 12 o'clock (warm-up, grace, lifetime) instead of filling up.
- **Liquid Glass (#1332)** — turns off UIKit compatibility mode and adopts real iOS 26 glass (`GlassChrome`) with a pre-26 material fallback, plus a glass tab bar with a centered treatment button.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a UI / layout / rendering change only — it does **not** touch the algorithm, dosing, or the Core Data predicates that feed oref.

## Additional Notes

The work here was already reviewed and merged part-by-part in #1326–#1332, each of which was independently shippable. This PR is the integration merge of that series onto `dev`. The commit history preserves the per-part boundaries if one wants to step through it.

includedPullRequests.title: Stop Crashlytics Uploads Immediately After Diagnostics Opt-Out
includedPullRequests.body:
`setCrashlyticsCollectionEnabled(false)` only gates future events. The FirebaseSessions event GoogleDataTransport already queued stays on disk and GDT retries it for seven days, so firebaselogging-pa.googleapis.com still shows up in App Privacy Report minutes after opting out.

Route both call sites through `CrashReportingGate: purge` GDT's store when a Trio user opts out, and skip `FirebaseApp.configure()` on any later launches so nothing can re-queue or upload queued sessions. 

Trio’s opt-out-by-default stays unchanged.

Fixes #1372.
